evals.query: I have a CreateUserRequest record in my Kora 2.0 service. How do I validate that name is not blank, email matches a regex, and age is between 18 and 120?
expected_behavior: Annotates the record type with @Valid from io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation
Uses @NotBlank on name, @Pattern("...") on email (value is the unnamed attribute, there is no regexp attribute), and @Range(from = 18, to = 120) on age
Notes that @Valid generates $CreateUserRequest_Validator and registers Validator<CreateUserRequest> in the graph, and that the interface is what you inject
Uses the io.koraframework group and never ru.tinkoff.kora, jakarta.validation or javax.validation
Does not introduce a @NotNull constraint — nullability is implicit and opted out with JSpecify @Nullable

evals.query: I added jakarta.validation @NotBlank and @Email to my Kora record and the annotation processor runs fine, but the DTO is never validated at runtime. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies that Kora validation is NOT Jakarta/JSR-380 — jakarta.validation.* and javax.validation.* annotations are unrecognised, produce no generated code and no diagnostic
Replaces them with io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation.* constraints
States there is no @Email constraint in Kora and maps it to @Pattern with an email regex
Does not suggest adding a jakarta.validation-api dependency, a Hibernate Validator provider, or a jakarta ConstraintValidator
Does not claim the annotation processor would have reported an error

evals.query: Which validation constraints ship with Kora 2.0? I need a minimum value, a UUID check and an enum-like set of allowed strings.
expected_behavior: Does not claim the constraint set is only @NotBlank/@NotEmpty/@Pattern/@Range/@Size — Kora 2.0 ships 22 constraints
Uses @Min (long value) for the minimum, @UUID for the identifier and @OneOf({"A","B"}) for the allowed set, all from io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation
Mentions further built-ins that exist, such as @Max, @Positive/@Negative, @Digits, @AssertTrue/@AssertFalse, @Past/@Future, @Url and @Uri
States that @Valid on an enum is a compile error ("Validation can't be generated for enum") so @OneOf is applied to the raw string
Does not invent constraints such as @Email, @NotNull, @CreditCardNumber or jakarta equivalents

evals.query: How do I make a Kora 2.0 service method validate its arguments before it runs?
expected_behavior: Adds @Validate to the method and annotates parameters (e.g. @Valid on a DTO param, @NotBlank/@Pattern on scalars)
Explains the aspect throws io.koraframework.validation.common.ViolationException before the body when validation fails
States the class must be non-final with a non-private constructor and the method non-final and non-private (Java), or open (Kotlin), because the proxy is $Name__AopProxy extends Name
Does not invent a @Validated annotation — Kora has only @Validate — and does not rely on field injection

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 Java build fails with "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class 'com.example.OrdersService' because the class is final". I only added @Validate to one method.
expected_behavior: Explains that a final class, a final method or a private method carrying @Validate is a hard compile error in Java, because the generated $Name__AopProxy must extend the class and override the method
Fixes it by removing final from the class (and from the method), keeping the method at least package-private and leaving a non-private constructor
Notes Kotlin behaves the same way, reporting "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class '...' because the class is not open"
Does not claim that Java silently skips a final class or that javac exits 0 — that is only true for an abstract class or an interface, which Java skips without a diagnostic while Kotlin rejects it
Does not suggest enabling a runtime proxy, a CGLIB/ByteBuddy setting, or an extra compiler flag — Kora AOP is compile-time only
Does not tell the user to reference the generated $Name__AopProxy class directly

evals.query: KSP fails on my Kora Kotlin service with "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class 'com.example.OrdersService' because the class is not open". I only added @Validate to one function.
expected_behavior: Marks BOTH the class `open class` and the annotated function `open fun` — either one alone is insufficient
Explains the generated proxy subclasses the service, which is why Kotlin's default final classes and members break it
Keeps ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") as the processor rather than a Java annotationProcessor
Does not suggest all-open/kotlin-allopen compiler plugins or making the class abstract
Does not claim the error can be ignored

evals.query: I added Kora validation annotations to my Kotlin data class but nothing is ever validated. The build is green.
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing @field: use-site target and rewrites the constraints as @field:NotBlank, @field:Size(...), @field:Pattern(...)
Explains the constraint annotations declare METHOD/FIELD/PARAMETER targets but not PROPERTY, so Kotlin's default puts them on the constructor parameter where the generated validator does not look
Uses Kotlin nullable types (String?) for optional fields instead of any @Nullable annotation, and writes @Range attributes as doubles (from = 18.0, to = 120.0)
Notes a data class is fine for class validation; open is only needed when the class hosts a @Validate method
Does not use jakarta.validation annotations or ru.tinkoff.kora packages

evals.query: I put @NotBlank and @Range on the getters of a plain (non-record) Kora class annotated with @Valid, and the generated validator does nothing.
expected_behavior: Explains that for a plain class the processor reads constraints from the FIELDS, and constraints on getters are silently ignored — the generated validator contains only the root null check
Moves the constraints onto the fields while keeping JavaBean getters, which is what the generated validator calls (value.getName())
Notes that records are different: the component annotation is propagated to the backing field and the accessor used is name()
Does not suggest switching to reflection, adding @Target(METHOD) manually, or annotating the constructor parameters instead

evals.query: My OrderRequest contains a Customer object and a List of OrderItem. How do I get Kora 2.0 to validate the nested objects and collection elements too?
expected_behavior: Marks each nested type (Customer, OrderItem) with @Valid so a Validator<T> is generated for each
Adds @Valid on the nested field/parameter including the List, and explains ValidatorModule derives Validator<List<T>>/Validator<Set<T>>/Validator<Collection<T>> from Validator<T>
Explains violation paths are dotted with bracketed indices, e.g. customer.address.city and items.[0].productId via Violation.path().full()
Does not rely on jakarta.validation cascade semantics or on reflective traversal

evals.query: When a request fails validation in my Kora 2.0 HTTP service it returns 500. I already have ValidationModule on my @KoraApp. How do I turn ViolationException into a structured 400 response?
expected_behavior: Explains ValidationModule declares ValidationHttpServerInterceptor as an untagged @DefaultComponent, so nothing picks it up — the router collects @Tag(HttpServer.class) All<HttpServerInterceptor>

Overrides the module method with @Tag(HttpServer.class) where HttpServer is io.koraframework.http.server.common.HttpServer, and supplies a ViolationExceptionHttpServerResponseMapper that returns HttpServerResponse.of(400, HttpBody.json(...))

Describes the two roles correctly: ValidationHttpServerInterceptor is the HttpServerInterceptor that catches ViolationException; ViolationExceptionHttpServerResponseMapper is an optional collaborator that shapes the body, and without it the interceptor still answers 400 with HttpServerResponseException.of(400, message)
Builds the error body from exception.getViolations() using Violation.message() and Violation.path().full(), and serialises with JsonWriter.toByteArray(...) — never toByteArrayUnchecked
Does not use @Tag(HttpServerModule.class), which is the Kora 1.x tag that still compiles while the interceptor silently never runs
Does not hand-roll a try/catch in every controller method, and does not register the mapper as an HttpServerResponseMapper

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 Kotlin app I am overriding validationHttpServerInterceptor to tag it for the HTTP server, but the compiler says "'validationHttpServerInterceptor' overrides nothing".
expected_behavior: Identifies the nullability mismatch: the Java module declares the parameter @Nullable under JSpecify, so the Kotlin override must be ViolationExceptionHttpServerResponseMapper?
Shows the corrected override with @Tag(HttpServer::class) and the nullable parameter type
Notes the error message never mentions nullability, which is why the cause is easy to miss
Does not suggest removing the override keyword, adding @JvmName, or carrying Java nullability annotations into Kotlin

evals.query: I need Kora 2.0 validation in a batch job with no HTTP server. Which artifact and module should I use, and will validation-module drag an HTTP server onto my classpath?
expected_behavior: Recommends io.koraframework:validation-common with io.koraframework.validation.common.constraint.ValidatorModule for a non-HTTP application

States correctly that validation-module does NOT bring http-server-common with it — the dependency is compileOnly (requires static in module-info) and the published 2.0.0.RC2 POM and Gradle module metadata list only validation-common and jspecify
Notes that ValidationModule extends ValidatorModule and would still compile in a non-HTTP app (the untagged interceptor is simply pruned), but ValidatorModule is the right choice for intent
Keeps the mandatory processor: annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (or ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors") and resolves versions through io.koraframework:kora-bom
Does not claim ValidationModule transitively pulls in an HTTP server artifact, and does not tell the user to exclude http-server-common

evals.query: Can Kora 2.0 validation stop at the first error instead of collecting all violations?
expected_behavior: For methods, uses @Validate(failFast = true)
For manual validation, uses ValidationContext.failFast() or ValidationContext.builder().failFast(true).build() and passes it to validator.validate(value, context) / validateAndThrow(value, context)
Explains the default collects every violation into one ViolationException, and that the fail-fast flag propagates into nested validators and collection elements through the context
Clarifies that ValidationContext is validation-scoped path/fail-fast state, not the Kora 1.x Context propagation type, which no longer exists in Kora 2.0
Does not invent validation groups or a failOnFirst property

evals.query: I need a custom Kora 2.0 constraint annotation @Prefixed(prefix = "ME", minLength = 4) for String fields. How do I build one?
expected_behavior: Implements Validator<String> returning List<Violation> built with context.violates(...) and handling null

Declares a named ValidatorFactory sub-interface with a create(String prefix, int minLength) overload — one parameter per annotation attribute, in declaration order — because Kora 2.0 does pass annotation attributes to the factory
Registers the factory as a @KoraApp default method returning PrefixedValidator::new, on a module that still extends ValidatorModule or ValidationModule

Declares the annotation with @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS), a @Target covering METHOD/FIELD/PARAMETER, and @ValidatedBy(PrefixedValidatorFactory.class) from io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation
Does not claim annotation attributes cannot reach the validator, and does not use jakarta ConstraintValidator / @Constraint
Mentions the compile error on arity mismatch: "Expected PrefixedValidatorFactory#create() method with 2 parameters, but was didn't find such"

evals.query: How do I validate the return value of a Kora 2.0 method — the returned List must have at least one element and each element must be valid?
expected_behavior: Puts @Validate on the method to enable the aspect, @Valid on the method to validate the returned objects, and @Size on the method to constrain the list, supplying max because @Size.max() has no default
Explains result validation runs after the body produces the value and that constraints for the result go on the METHOD, not the parameters
States that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous: Publisher (Mono/Flux) and Future return types are rejected by @Validate with a processing error; Kotlin additionally supports suspend and Flow<T>
Does not present Mono/Flux or reactive repositories as a supported Kora 2.0 contract, and does not invent a class-level @Validated annotation

evals.query: Can I validate my Kora 2.0 @ConfigSource configuration so a bad application.conf fails at startup instead of at first use?
expected_behavior: Adds @Valid to the @ConfigSource (or @ConfigMapper) interface alongside the constraint annotations on its accessor methods
Explains the generated config mapper then calls validateAndThrow on the parsed value, so an invalid config fails during graph build with a ViolationException
Notes @Valid on a plain interface is a compile error ("Validation can't be generated for non sealed interface") — config interfaces and sealed interfaces are the supported interface shapes
Keeps the config annotations as io.koraframework.config.common.annotation.@ConfigSource / @ConfigMapper and does not mention the removed Kora 1.x @ConfigValueExtractor
Does not confuse the constraint io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation.Size with the config value type io.koraframework.common.util.Size
